title: Right-exact conormal sequence for two closed immersions
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ be closed immersions with $f\circ i=j$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], with ideal sheaves $\mathcal I_i,\mathcal I_j$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Put $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=i^*\mathcal I_i$ and $\mathcal C_{Z/Y}=j^*\mathcal I_j$ [def-pc-module-pullback], and let $\Omega^1_{X/Y}$ be the relative differential sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. There is a canonical right-exact sequence of $\mathcal O_Z$-modules
$$\mathcal C_{Z/Y}\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal C_{Z/X}\xrightarrow{v}i^*\Omega^1_{X/Y}\longrightarrow0.$$
Here $u$ is exactly the canonical conormal morphism of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-conormal-functorial] for the square with top map $1_Z$ and bottom map $f$. Locally the map $v$ sends the class of a local equation $a\in\mathcal I_i$ to $1\otimes\mathrm d_{X/Y}a$. Right exactness means that $v$ is surjective as a sheaf morphism and its kernel is the sheaf image of $u$. No finite-type, smoothness, flatness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Construct $v$ globally. For a local equation $a\in\mathcal I_i(U)$, take $\mathrm d_{X/Y}a$ and then its pullback-unit image in $\Gamma(i^{-1}U,i^*\Omega^1_{X/Y})$. This defines a morphism of additive sheaves $t:\mathcal I_i\to i_*i^*\Omega^1_{X/Y}$. For $b\in\mathcal O_X(U)$ the Leibniz identity gives $t(ba)=i^*b\,t(a)+i^*a\,i^*(\mathrm db)=i^*b\,t(a)$, since $i^*a=0$. Thus $t$ is $\mathcal O_X$-linear. The pullback adjunction supplies $v:i^*\mathcal I_i\to i^*\Omega^1_{X/Y}$ with the required formula. Restrictions commute with the derivation and the pullback unit, so this construction is global and canonical. In particular $t(ab)=0$ for $a,b\in\mathcal I_i$, explaining its dependence only on the conormal class.

source.place: Tag 01UZ (lemma-differentials-relative-immersion), construction of the first arrow, as used in Tag 067L.

proof.text: Take $u$ to be the canonical map of the conormal-functoriality node, applied with ambient map $f$ and map $1_Z$ on the closed subschemes. Its hypotheses are exactly $f\circ i=j$ and the two given closed immersions. On equation classes it sends $a$ to $f^\sharp(a)$. Since $\mathrm d_{X/Y}(f^\sharp a)=0$, the composite $vu$ vanishes on these classes and hence on their $\mathcal O_Z$-linear combinations. They locally generate the pullback of the ideal sheaf, so $vu=0$.

proof.text: Fix $z\in Z$, put $x=i(z)$, $y=j(z)$, and set $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $C=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$. The closed immersions give surjections $A\to C$ and $B\to C$: on affine charts they are quotients, and a fraction in a quotient local ring lifts by lifting its numerator and denominator. The triangle makes the former map the composite $A\to B\to C$. Put $I=\ker(A\to C)$, $J=\ker(B\to C)$. The inclusion of each ideal sheaf remains injective on stalks by clause (1) of the module-stalk-exactness node, so its stalk identifies with its range in the local ring. The ideal-stalk-range node identifies $(\mathcal I_j)_y=I$ and $(\mathcal I_i)_x=J$. The pullback-stalk node then gives $(\mathcal C_{Z/Y})_z=I\otimes_A C$ and $(\mathcal C_{Z/X})_z=J\otimes_B C$. Identify the latter tensor with $J/J^2$ by $b\otimes\bar r\mapsto rb\bmod J^2$, inverse $b\bmod J^2\mapsto b\otimes1$; changing $r$ by an element of $J$ changes $rb$ by an element of $J^2$, and $(bb')\otimes1=b\otimes\bar b'=0$ for $b,b'\in J$. These formulas are inverse on pure tensors. The identical calculation for $I$ identifies the first tensor with $I/I^2$.

source.place: Tags 01R3 (lemma-affine-conormal) and 067L: local conormal calculation; Sheaves Tag 0098 (lemma-stalk-pullback-modules).

proof.text: The differential-stalk comparison identifies $(\Omega^1_{X/Y})_x$ with $\Omega_{B/A}$, sending the germ of $\mathrm da$ to $\mathrm d(a_x)$. Apply the pullback-stalk isomorphism once more to obtain $(i^*\Omega^1_{X/Y})_z\cong C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}$, using tensor symmetry. Under step 3 and these isomorphisms the stalk of $u$ is $a\bmod I^2\mapsto\alpha(a)\bmod J^2$, where $\alpha:A\to B$: this follows from the equation-class formula for conormal functoriality by taking germs. The stalk of $v$ is $b\bmod J^2\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm db$, by step 1 and the germ-of-unit formula in the pullback-stalk node. These identities hold on every class, since every ideal-stalk element is represented by a local equation.

Apply the ring two-quotients sequence to $A\to B\to C$ from step 3. Its only extra hypothesis, surjectivity of $A\to C$, has already been verified. Step 4 identifies its two arrows with the stalk maps of the constructed sheaf sequence, so $v_z$ is surjective and $\ker(v_z)=\operatorname{im}(u_z)$ for every $z$. The module-stalk-exactness node, applied to the complex from step 2, now proves exactness at $\mathcal C_{Z/X}$. Applied also to $\mathcal C_{Z/X}\to i^*\Omega^1_{X/Y}\to0$, it proves that $v$ is a sheaf epimorphism. This is precisely the stated right exactness. For empty $Z$ both stalk tests are vacuous and all three sheaves are zero.
